answer: Agents selling karst maps, ocean forecasts or nebula images must enroll a hardware-backed key. A verifier checks the chip manufacturer's certificate and a fresh signed challenge, then records a hash of the device identity. Only one active agent key may be bound to that hash; replacing a key revokes the old slot. Generating a thousand software keys therefore buys no extra slots: a farm needs a thousand certified chips. This creates a hardware cost, not proof of honest behavior, and depends on the issuer refusing counterfeit certificates.
